lesson.title: Map provider duties and release gates
lesson.summary: Map provider duties and leave unproved market-entry gates visible.

prerequisites.reason: They require the relevant high-risk route.

blocks: A **provider duty map** allocates Article 16 tasks to an accountable actor. For the applicable full high-risk regime it includes system requirements, a quality-management system, documentation and controlled logs, correction and information, and conformity evidence for authorities.

A quality-management system is the documented organisational process for ensuring compliance. The next lesson develops it. Do not apply this full map automatically to the limited Annex I Section B route.

blocks: Market-entry gates include the relevant Article 43 conformity-assessment procedure before supply/service, an Article 47 EU declaration of conformity, Article 48 CE marking and applicable Article 49 registration.

A conformity assessment demonstrates specified compliance; the declaration states conformity and CE marking communicates it. This lesson identifies the gates. Selecting the actual procedure, assessment body, marking method and registration category needs the later market-entry course and the applicable product facts.

blocks: **Provider identity** must be indicated on the system or, where not possible, on packaging or accompanying documentation as applicable: name, registered trade name or trademark, and contact address.
A logo with no contact address does not establish this item. Record whose identity appears and where. The identified provider must still fulfil the other applicable obligations.

blocks: **Provider accessibility** under Article 16(l) concerns compliance in accordance with Directives 2016/2102 and 2019/882. Establish their scope and relevant national implementing rules rather than inventing one universal AI certificate.

The Web Accessibility Directive concerns websites/apps of public-sector bodies. The European Accessibility Act covers specified products and services, including certain computers, banking and e-commerce. A commercial product needs its actual category tested; not every website has identical directive obligations.

blocks: Case: Northbridge has a name/address record but no conformity-route evidence and no accessibility-scope analysis. Identity alone does not close its provider map.
Keep the missing gates, relevant sources and responsible owners in the dossier. Do not treat a supplier’s general “compliant” declaration as proof that each applicable gate has been discharged.
